items: List the five pillars of a Well-Architected Framework.
Explain operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, and cost optimization.
Apply the pillars as a review lens for any architecture.
Recognize that trade-offs between pillars are a normal SA responsibility.
Well-Architected Framework — a structured set of best practices for building secure, resilient, efficient, and cost-effective systems.
Operational Excellence — running and monitoring systems to deliver business value and continuously improve.
Security — protecting data, systems, and assets through identity, detection, and protection.
Reliability — the ability to recover from failures and meet availability/throughput demands.
Performance Efficiency — using computing resources efficiently to meet requirements as they change.
Cost Optimization — avoiding unnecessary expense and selecting the right resources.

blocks.text: A Well-Architected Framework gives an SA a shared, repeatable vocabulary to evaluate designs. It prevents "hero architecture" — solutions that work only because one person holds the whole design in their head — and instead produces systems that are reviewable, measurable, and improvable.

Operational Excellence focuses on running and monitoring systems to deliver business value and continually improving processes and procedures. Questions include: how do we detect failures, and how do we respond?

Security is about protecting information and systems. It rests on six areas: identity and access management, detective controls, infrastructure protection, data protection, incident response, and applying security at all layers. The principle of least privilege is central.

Reliability requires a system to perform its intended function correctly and consistently, recovering from infrastructure or service failures and adapting to changing load. This covers foundational requirements (network, compute), change management, and failure management.

Performance Efficiency is the ability to use computing resources efficiently to meet system requirements, and to maintain that efficiency as demand changes and technology evolves. It emphasizes selecting the right resource types and sizes, and going global when needed.

Cost Optimization is the ability to run systems to deliver business value at the lowest price point. It means understanding where money is spent, selecting the right resource types, analyzing spend over time, and managing demand.

No design maximizes every pillar simultaneously. A highly reliable, secure system may cost more; an aggressively cost-optimized system may sacrifice some resilience. The SA's job is to make these trade-offs explicit and align them with business priorities.
